findings: l.3326-3330: the conclusion 'M(S) = Gamma\Omega(S~) is a linear twisted product over a Misner spacetime' is false for Gamma itself; it holds up to finite index. Counterexample in M^4 (form xy+|z|^2, coordinates (x,z1,z2,y)): gamma0(x,z,y) = (e^-1 x, z, e y), sigma(x,z1,z2,y) = (-y, z1+1, -z2, -x) (SO0-affine, spacelike elliptic, allowed by Rem 8.9), sigma gamma0 sigma^-1 = gamma0^-1; Gamma = <gamma0, sigma> acts freely and properly on Omega = {x>0,y<0} x R^2, Sigma = {xy=-1} ∩ Omega satisfies (CC'), Omega(S~) = Omega; <gamma0, sigma^2> has index 2 and fixes Delta_0, so Gamma is elementary; the direction of U contains the (x,y)-plane, so Gamma_U is non-abelian, while a Misner group (misnerGroup L) is abelian, and quotient presentations of a convex domain are conjugate. Found by the read-only audit; statement restated for a finite-index Gamma'.
